/-!
# Conjecture 10.11

by R. I. Grigorchuk

Is it true that every finitely presented group contains either a free subsemigroup on two
generators or a nilpotent subgroup of finite index?

A group is finitely presented if it is isomorphic to a group given by finitely many generators
and finitely many defining relators. Two elements $a, b$ of a group generate a free subsemigroup
on two generators if distinct nonempty positive words in $a$ and $b$ always represent distinct
group elements, i.e. the canonical semigroup homomorphism from the free semigroup of rank $2$ is
injective. The "or" is inclusive.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

blocks.name: IsFinitelyPresented
blocks.text:
/-- A group $G$ is finitely presented if it is isomorphic to `PresentedGroup rels` for a finite
set of generators `α` and a finite set of relators `rels : Set (FreeGroup α)`. -/
def IsFinitelyPresented (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (α : Type) (rels : Set (FreeGroup α)),
    Finite α ∧ rels.Finite ∧ Nonempty (G ≃* PresentedGroup rels)

blocks.docstring:
Two elements $a, b$ of a group $G$ generate a free subsemigroup on two generators if the
semigroup homomorphism from the free semigroup on two generators sending the generators to
$a$ and $b$ is injective, i.e. $a$ and $b$ satisfy no nontrivial positive-word relation.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `Subsemigroup.closure {a, b}` (only 2-generated, not freeness); `FreeMonoid.lift` injectivity (equivalent but less literal than the semigroup version); `IsFreeGroup`/`FreeGroup.lift` (wrong structure: groups, not semigroups).
justification.name: Kourovka.«10.11».IsFreeSubsemigroupPair
justification.why_needed: Mathlib has `FreeSemigroup` and `FreeSemigroup.lift` but no predicate saying that two elements of a semigroup/group generate a free subsemigroup with them as a basis. The definition is `Function.Injective (FreeSemigroup.lift ![a, b])`.

blocks.name: IsFreeSubsemigroupPair
blocks.text:
/-- Two elements $a, b$ of a group $G$ generate a free subsemigroup on two generators if the
semigroup homomorphism from the free semigroup on two generators sending the generators to
$a$ and $b$ is injective, i.e. $a$ and $b$ satisfy no nontrivial positive-word relation. -/
def IsFreeSubsemigroupPair {G : Type*} [Group G] (a b : G) : Prop :=

theorem isFinitelyPresented_presentedGroup {α : Type} [Finite α] {rels : Set (FreeGroup α)}

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem not_isFreeSubsemigroupPair_of_commGroup {G : Type*} [CommGroup G] (a b : G) :
    ¬ IsFreeSubsemigroupPair a b := by
  intro h
  have := @h (.of 0 * .of 1) (.of 1 * .of 0) (by simp [mul_comm])
  simp [FreeSemigroup.ext_iff] at this

claims.decomposer_note: Single yes/no question (Grigorchuk's dichotomy for finitely presented groups), to be stated as `answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], finitely presented G → (∃ a b : G, a and b generate a free subsemigroup of rank 2, i.e. the canonical map from the free monoid/semigroup on two generators is injective) ∨ (∃ H : Subgroup G, H.FiniteIndex ∧ H is nilpotent)`; 'finitely presented' must be expressed via a finite generating set and finitely many relators (e.g. G ≃* PresentedGroup rels with Finite α and Set.Finite rels), the 'or' is inclusive, and 'free subsemigroup on two generators' means a genuinely free semigroup of rank 2 (the two elements a, b satisfy no nontrivial positive-word relation), not merely a 2-generated subsemigroup.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the same faithful proposition: answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ finitely presented G (G ≃* PresentedGroup rels with Finite α and rels.Finite), either ∃ a b with the canonical map from the free semigroup/monoid on two letters injective, or ∃ finite-index nilpotent subgroup (inclusive ∨). The FreeMonoid (c02,c03,c07) and FreeSemigroup (others) variants are equivalent in a group (a nonempty positive word equal to 1 gives w·a = a with w·a ≠ a as words). c01 is chosen for style: it uses Mathlib's `Group.IsVirtuallyNilpotent` (verified by #print to be definitionally `∃ N : Subgroup G, IsNilpotent N ∧ N.FiniteIndex`, exactly the requested shape), gives both non-Mathlib notions named bespoke definitions with docstrings, and includes API tests for each (as CONTRIBUTING.md asks). The file compiles with only the `declaration uses 'sorry'` warning; used unchanged.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 10.11

by R. I. Grigorchuk

Is it true that every finitely presented group contains either a free subsemigroup on two
generators or a nilpotent subgroup of finite index?

A group is finitely presented if it is isomorphic to a group given by finitely many generators
and finitely many defining relators. Two elements $a, b$ of a group generate a free subsemigroup
on two generators if distinct nonempty positive words in $a$ and $b$ always represent distinct
group elements, i.e. the canonical semigroup homomorphism from the free semigroup of rank $2$ is
injective. The "or" is inclusive.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«10.11»

/-- A group $G$ is finitely presented if it is isomorphic to `PresentedGroup rels` for a finite
set of generators `α` and a finite set of relators `rels : Set (FreeGroup α)`. -/
def IsFinitelyPresented (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (α : Type) (rels : Set (FreeGroup α)),
    Finite α ∧ rels.Finite ∧ Nonempty (G ≃* PresentedGroup rels)

/-- Two elements $a, b$ of a group $G$ generate a free subsemigroup on two generators if the
semigroup homomorphism from the free semigroup on two generators sending the generators to
$a$ and $b$ is injective, i.e. $a$ and $b$ satisfy no nontrivial positive-word relation. -/
def IsFreeSubsemigroupPair {G : Type*} [Group G] (a b : G) : Prop :=
  Function.Injective (FreeSemigroup.lift ![a, b])

/-- A group given by a finite presentation is finitely presented. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isFinitelyPresented_presentedGroup {α : Type} [Finite α] {rels : Set (FreeGroup α)}
    (h : rels.Finite) : IsFinitelyPresented (PresentedGroup rels) :=
  ⟨α, rels, inferInstance, h, ⟨MulEquiv.refl _⟩⟩

/-- No two elements of a commutative group generate a free subsemigroup on two generators. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem not_isFreeSubsemigroupPair_of_commGroup {G : Type*} [CommGroup G] (a b : G) :
    ¬ IsFreeSubsemigroupPair a b := by
  intro h
  have := @h (.of 0 * .of 1) (.of 1 * .of 0) (by simp [mul_comm])
  simp [FreeSemigroup.ext_iff] at this

/--
Is it true that every finitely presented group contains either a free subsemigroup on two
generators or a nilpotent subgroup of finite index?

Here `Group.IsVirtuallyNilpotent G` means that `G` has a nilpotent subgroup of finite index.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«10.11» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsFinitelyPresented G →
      (∃ a b : G, IsFreeSubsemigroupPair a b) ∨ Group.IsVirtuallyNilpotent G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«10.11»

items: Groups are quantified over `Type` (universe 0), following the Kourovka file idiom (1_40, 19_25); this loses nothing since finitely presented groups are countable and the definition of `IsFinitelyPresented` works for any universe.

`IsFinitelyPresented G` is `∃ (α : Type) (rels : Set (FreeGroup α)), Finite α ∧ rels.Finite ∧ Nonempty (G ≃* PresentedGroup rels)`, i.e. isomorphic to a group with finitely many generators and finitely many relators (α may be empty, giving the trivial group, which is harmless).

'Free subsemigroup on two generators' is read literally as a free *semigroup* (not monoid) of rank 2: `Function.Injective (FreeSemigroup.lift ![a, b])`, i.e. distinct nonempty positive words in a, b give distinct elements. This forces a ≠ b and is equivalent to the free-monoid version (a nonempty word equal to 1 would give w*a = a, contradicting injectivity).

'Nilpotent subgroup of finite index' uses Mathlib's `Group.IsVirtuallyNilpotent G`, definitionally `∃ N : Subgroup G, Group.IsNilpotent N ∧ N.FiniteIndex`, exactly the form requested by the decomposition table.
The disjunction is the inclusive `∨`, as the table specifies.
Two `@[category API]` tests are included: `PresentedGroup rels` with finite data is finitely presented, and no pair in a commutative group is a free subsemigroup pair.

reviewer_notes: Sanity checks performed in scratch files: `FreeSemigroup.lift ![a, b] : FreeSemigroup (Fin 2) →ₙ* G`; injectivity is refuted by a = b and by a sample positive-word relation a*b = b*a*a; the trivial group (empty generator type, empty relator set) is finitely presented and every finite group is virtually nilpotent via ⊥, so boundary cases behave as the mathematics requires. `answer(True)` = the dichotomy holds for all finitely presented groups; `answer(False)` = some finitely presented group is a counterexample. Quantifying G over `Type` follows the sibling Kourovka files and loses nothing since finitely presented groups are countable. No candidate omitted the slot and no objections to the decomposition were raised; I agree the single-slot table matches the source. A reviewer might prefer moving `IsFinitelyPresented` to FormalConjecturesForMathlib as a reusable definition; it is kept in the problem file here since the deliverable is a single file.
